title: Feast Of Pentecost
body:
15 Minutes w/ The Captains · 2026-06-03

Opens [Exod 23](/bible/exodus/23) · [Lev 23](/bible/leviticus/23) · [Num 28](/bible/numbers/28) · [Deut 16](/bible/deuteronomy/16) · [2 Chr 8](/bible/2-chronicles/8) · [2 Chr 31](/bible/2-chronicles/31) · [Tobit 2](/bible/tobit/2) · [Acts 2](/bible/acts/2) · [Acts 20](/bible/acts/20) · [Col 2](/bible/colossians/2)
## Introduction *[[0:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=16s)]* Today's lesson is on the feast of Pentecost. Pentecost is a Greek word, so we will not see it in the Old Testament, which is written in Hebrew. What we will see is the feast of harvest and the feast of weeks, which is the same feast. Our forefathers kept it as kings and in captivity, the apostles kept it after Christ, and we continue to keep it today in the faith of Jesus Christ, without animal sacrifice. ## Scriptures Opened **[Exodus 23:14-17](/bible/exodus/23#v14)** *[[0:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=29s)]* > [14](/bible/exodus/23#v14) Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year. > > [15](/bible/exodus/23#v15) Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread: (thou shalt eat unleavened bread seven days, as I commanded thee, in the time appointed of the month Abib; for in it thou camest out from Egypt: and none shall appear before me empty:) > > [16](/bible/exodus/23#v16) And the feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, which thou hast sown in the field: and the feast of ingathering, which is in the end of the year, when thou hast gathered in thy labours out of the field. > > [17](/bible/exodus/23#v17) Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord God. - Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: these are not the only three feasts, but these are the three major feasts. - Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread: this is also known as the Passover. - And the feast of harvest: the word Pentecost is a Greek word. The Old Testament is written in Hebrew, so we will not see the word Pentecost in the Old Testament. But we will see the feast of harvest, which is the same feast. - And the feast of ingathering, which is in the end of the year: we call that the feast of tabernacles. - Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord GOD: and where do we appear before the Lord our God? We report back to Jerusalem. **[Leviticus 23:15-16](/bible/leviticus/23#v15)** *[[2:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=120s)]* > [15](/bible/leviticus/23#v15) And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete: > > [16](/bible/leviticus/23#v16) Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days; and ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the Lord. - From the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering: we offer that after the Passover, and we count seven Sabbaths after that. - Seven sabbaths shall be complete: seven Sabbaths, seven days per week, that's 49 days. Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days: 49 plus one equals 50 days. That's where we get Pentecost from. Pentecost always falls on Saturday sundown until Sunday sundown according to this commandment. - And ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the LORD: under the old covenant, we offered sacrifice on the feast of Pentecost. **[Numbers 28:26-27](/bible/numbers/28#v26)** *[[3:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=189s)]* > [26](/bible/numbers/28#v26) Also in the day of the firstfruits, when ye bring a new meat offering unto the Lord, after your weeks be out, ye shall have an holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work: > > [27](/bible/numbers/28#v27) But ye shall offer the burnt offering for a sweet savour unto the Lord; two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of the first year; - In the day of the firstfruits: that's the feast of Pentecost. When ye bring a new meat offering unto the LORD, after your weeks be out: after seven weeks. - Ye shall have an holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work: that's the day we come together for fellowship. That's not the day to cut the grass, to work overtime, to do chores around the house. It is a Sabbath day. - Two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of the first year: so under the old covenant we come together to fellowship, we offer animal sacrifice, and we do no work. **[Deuteronomy 16:16](/bible/deuteronomy/16#v16)** *[[4:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=253s)]* > [16](/bible/deuteronomy/16#v16) Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles: and they shall not appear before the Lord empty: - In the place which he shall choose: the place that the Lord chose is Jerusalem, according to 2 Chronicles. - And in the feast of weeks: so it was called the feast of harvest, and it's called the feast of weeks. Why? Because we count seven weeks. And they shall not appear before the LORD empty. **[2 Chronicles 8:12-13](/bible/2-chronicles/8#v12)** *[[4:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=295s)]* > [12](/bible/2-chronicles/8#v12) Then Solomon offered burnt offerings unto the Lord on the altar of the Lord, which he had built before the porch, > > [13](/bible/2-chronicles/8#v13) Even after a certain rate every day, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. - Are we the only ones that keep the feast of weeks, the feast of harvest, the feast of Pentecost? No. Let's find out what King Solomon did. - Solomon offered burnt offerings unto the LORD on the altar of the LORD: King Solomon built an altar unto the Lord and offered sacrifices on it. Even after a certain rate every day: every day, in the morning and in the evening. - On the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year: so King Solomon kept the feast of weeks, the feast of Pentecost, and he offered sacrifices on those days. **[2 Chronicles 31:2-3](/bible/2-chronicles/31#v2)** *[[6:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=363s)]* > [2](/bible/2-chronicles/31#v2) And Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites after their courses, every man according to his service, the priests and Levites for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to minister, and to give thanks, and to praise in the gates of the tents of the Lord. > > [3](/bible/2-chronicles/31#v3) He appointed also the king’s portion of his substance for the burnt offerings, to wit, for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the sabbaths, and for the new moons, and for the set feasts, as it is written in the law of the Lord. - After King Solomon we had a lot of evil kings in the nation of Israel, but when King Hezekiah stepped up, he set things back in order. - For the morning and evening burnt offerings: we just read about King Solomon establishing the same thing. And the burnt offerings for the sabbaths, and for the new moons, and for the set feasts, as it is written in the law of the LORD: we just read that in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. - So when our brothers were in rulership as kings over the nation of Israel, we kept God's feasts. But when we were in captivity, we kept the feast as well. **[Tobit 2:1](/bible/tobit/2#v1)** *[[7:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=440s)]* > [1](/bible/tobit/2#v1) Now when I was come home again, and my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks, there was a good dinner prepared me, in the which I sat down to eat. - In the feast of Pentecost: one thing about the Israelites, even in the midst of captivity, we always find our way back to the laws of God, back to the feasts the Lord set up for us, for our good. We don't celebrate the feasts of our destruction set up by our enemies. - Which is the holy feast of the seven weeks, there was a good dinner prepared me: it's supposed to be a holy convocation and a good dinner. We going to eat good on the feast of Pentecost. **[Acts 2:1](/bible/acts/2#v1)** *[[8:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=502s)]* > [1](/bible/acts/2#v1) And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. - We were raised to believe that under the New Testament we don't got to celebrate what God set up for us; we get to celebrate what the white man set up for us. But after Christ died, resurrected and went back up to the Father, let's find out what the Israelites were still doing under Roman captivity. - And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place: why? We just read it in Deuteronomy 16 and 16. No matter where you are, you must report back to the place that the Lord chose, and that's exactly where they were on the day of Pentecost. **[Acts 20:16](/bible/acts/20#v16)** *[[9:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=562s)]* > [16](/bible/acts/20#v16) For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost. - Paul authored most of the New Testament. Let's see how Paul felt about the feast of Pentecost. - For he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost: Paul did everything in his power to keep the law we read about in Exodus 23 and Deuteronomy 16, to be in Jerusalem for the feast of Pentecost. - So why does a Christian in 2026 think Colossians 2 and 16 is telling us we don't have to celebrate the feast of Pentecost? Didn't Paul write the book of Colossians? Was Paul confused? Surely Paul's not confused. Surely the fake Christian in 2026 is confused. **[Colossians 2:16-17](/bible/colossians/2#v16)** *[[10:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=645s)]* > [16](/bible/colossians/2#v16) Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: > > [17](/bible/colossians/2#v17) Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. - Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink: the judgment happening at this time was the judgment and persecution for believing on Christ. Those that believed on Christ kept the commandments, but they did not offer animal sacrifice. So Paul is telling you, don't let anybody judge you for how you keep the feasts of the Lord. - Or in respect of an holyday: if you respect the holy day in honor of Christ, don't let anybody judge you for not offering animal sacrifice. Or of the new moon: Numbers chapter 28 tells us about the sacrifices that we offered on the new moon. Or of the sabbath days. - Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ: Christ's body represented that meat, and Christ's blood represented that drink offering. So in 2026 we continue to celebrate the feast of Pentecost, but we do so in the faith of Jesus Christ, the black Messiah. And since he was our sacrifice, we no longer offer animal sacrifices anymore. ## In Closing *[[12:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0&t=733s)]* Until next time, shalom. May Messiah Christ bless you all. --- [15 Minutes Index](/captains) · [Watch the full session on YouTube ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ip4IoxkINq0)
